Betroffene Personen und geänderte Arbeit: Ermitteln Sie, wer die Automatisierung nutzt, betreibt, unterstützt, genehmigt, konsumiert oder davon betroffen ist und welche Verantwortlichkeiten, Entscheidungen, Übergaben oder Arbeitsweisen sich ändern.
Aktivierung und Rollout-Ansatz: Steuern Sie Zugriff, Berechtigungen, Pilotnutzung, phasenweisen Rollout, eingeschränkte Gruppen, Parallelbetrieb und Rollout-Erweiterung.
Enablement und Support: Bereiten Sie Kommunikation, Schulung, Betriebsanweisungen und Supportwege vor.
Feedback und Kontrolle: Überwachen Sie Adoption, Vertrauen, tatsächliche Nutzung, Probleme und unerwartetes Verhalten und definieren Sie Auslöser für Pause, Rollback oder manuelle Bearbeitung.
Behandeln Sie den Rollout nicht als API-Veröffentlichung; konzentrieren Sie sich auf geänderte Arbeit, sichere Aktivierung, Vertrauen, Support und Adoption.
Beziehen Sie sowohl die vom Prozess betroffenen Nutzer als auch die für die Automatisierung verantwortlichen Betreiber ein.

resource.automation-opportunity-canvas.d: A compact primary canvas for linking optional supporting evidence to a testable automation hypothesis and validation decision.
resource.automation-opportunity-canvas.o: Supporting evidence, scope, assumptions, and validation experiment linked without duplicating other canvases
Evidence-based decision to proceed, revise, redesign the process, or reject
resource.automation-opportunity-canvas.s: State the automation hypothesis and reference Journey, Value Proposition, Domain, Business Impact, Capacity, or other evidence only where relevant.
Define the automation scope, out-of-scope work, and initial implementation hypothesis without making an architecture decision.
Identify critical assumptions, design the smallest useful validation experiment, and record the decision after reviewing evidence.
resource.automation-opportunity-canvas.t: Treat Customer Journey, Capability Value Proposition, Domain, Business Impact, and Capacity as optional supporting evidence, not required outputs for every automation opportunity.
Stop, narrow, or redesign weak opportunities before implementation choices become locked.
resource.human-automation-responsibility: A canvas for creating the initial allocation of what should be performed by people, rules, workflows, agents, systems, APIs, or UI automation.
Oversight, escalation, and audit evidence defined by process step
Implementation mechanisms selected without assuming every step should be automated
List the target process steps and current handoffs.
Assign each step to people, rules, workflows, agents, systems, APIs, UI automation, or a hybrid responsibility.
Define oversight, escalation, and evidence for each step so later architecture and workflow design can validate and refine the allocation.
Keep accountability visible even when execution is automated.
Revisit this canvas later only to validate architecture assumptions or refine workflow-level handoffs and exceptions.
resource.automation-workflow-canvas.desc: A canvas for designing the automation sequence, states, data, triggers, decisions, system interactions, failure paths, evidence, monitoring, and recovery.
resource.automation-workflow-canvas.outc: Triggers, stages, states, decisions, data, interactions, handoffs, exceptions, and recovery paths defined
Operational evidence and monitoring points identified before delivery
resource.automation-workflow-canvas.step: Separate the target process from the technical workflow.
Map triggers, inputs, stages, states, decisions, automation actions, system interactions, data sources, handoffs, outputs, and exceptions.
Define retries, timeouts, duplicate prevention, audit evidence, monitoring points, and recovery paths.
resource.automation-workflow-canvas.tips: Treat exceptions and manual recovery as part of the design, not an afterthought.
Revisit the Human-Automation Responsibility Canvas separately to refine responsibility allocation, oversight, escalation, and evidence for the workflow stages now being designed.
resource.automation-architecture-decisio: A canvas for comparing and justifying alternative implementation mechanisms for an automation solution.
Justified automation architecture and implementation approach
Candidate mechanisms compared on quality, risk, cost, skills, and operational fit
Markieren Sie jeden Kandidatenmechanismus als betrachtet, ausgewählt, abgelehnt oder nicht relevant, bevor Sie die tragfähigen Optionen vergleichen.
Evaluate feasibility, reliability, security, maintainability, latency, scalability, cost, vendor dependency, testability, observability, recoverability, skills, and architectural fit.
Document the preferred hybrid approach, rationale, risks, and open assumptions.
Do not force every mechanism into the solution; make irrelevant candidates explicit and compare only viable options.
Choose UI automation only when more stable system or integration paths are insufficient.
resource.automation-readiness-operations: A canvas for preparing the operating model for a safely released, supported, monitored, and recoverable automation.
Ownership, permissions, environments, evidence, monitoring, support, fallback, rollback, and risks prepared
Release readiness status and improvement backlog ready for readiness review and post-release learning
Prepare business owner, operational owner, affected users, permissions, credentials, environments, and documentation.
Prepare test evidence, exception handling, monitoring, support, manual fallback, rollback, and known risks.
Dokumentieren Sie den Release-Readiness-Status und den Verbesserungs-Backlog, ohne die formale Readiness-Entscheidung zu treffen.
Nutzen Sie dies während Delivery & Operations, um Nachweise vorzubereiten; nutzen Sie die Automatisierungs-Readiness-Checkliste für die formale Freigabeentscheidung.
Make manual fallback and operational ownership explicit before production use.
resource.user-operator-experience-requir: A cycle-specific view of experience, operational, and non-functional requirements for automation users, operators, approvers, and support teams.
Availability, timeliness, permissions, support, recovery, observability, and activation needs captured
Constraints ready for later architecture, workflow, and capacity decisions
Capture user, operator, approver, and support goals for the target process.
Clarify availability, timeliness, volume, data quality, permissions, activation, changes, support, observability, recovery, and continuity expectations.
Translate the expectations into constraints for later automation design without choosing the implementation mechanism.
Use this label in the Automation Cycle instead of API consumer wording.
Keep the shared underlying requirements canvas intact for other cycles.
resource.automation-monitoring-value-met: Anleitung zur Messung von Ergebnissen, operativer Leistung, Nutzerverhalten, Risiko, Wiederherstellung, realisiertem Wert, Hypothesenlernen und Lifecycle-Entscheidungen nach dem Rollout.
Automation monitoring, value, and learning evidence
Actual outcomes, run success, failure, exception, retry, intervention, processing time, waiting time, correction, incident, adoption, and benefit signals reviewed
Automation Hypothesis assumptions reviewed and improvement, expansion, redesign, or retirement decisions prioritized
Outcomes and value: compare expected process, user, and business outcomes with actual evidence.
Operational performance: review successful runs, failures, partial completions, exceptions, retries, timeouts, interventions, processing time, waiting time, and cost.
User, risk, and recovery signals: review errors, corrections, unsafe actions, bypassing, mistrust, support needs, fallback events, and recovery failures.
Learning and lifecycle decision: decide which hypothesis assumptions were supported or rejected and whether to improve, expand, restrict, redesign, pause, retire, or add backlog items.
Monitoring verwandelt operative, Nutzer-, Risiko- und Wertnachweise in Lifecycle-Entscheidungen und einen Verbesserungs-Backlog.
Include signals that show adoption, trust, human oversight needs, recovery needs, and realized value.
